resale_co.how_to_apply: No resale application is posted. The 1999 ordinance says a zoning permit from the Zoning Officer must be issued before a certificate of occupancy goes to a new occupant of an existing building; the Borough's zoning permit form is at https://shilohborough.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/SHL_ZONING_PERMIT.pdf. Contact the Housing Code Official (Teresa Warburton, Upper Deerfield Township, 856-455-9591) or the Borough office (856-455-3054, clerk@shilohborough.com) to arrange the certificate of occupancy.
resale_co.contact_title: Housing Code Official (Upper Deerfield Township, serving Shiloh)

resale_co.notes: The only Borough source found is the scanned Development Ordinance of 1979 as amended June 1, 1999 (read page by page from the image; no text layer). Section 4.17 says a zoning permit must be issued before a certificate of occupancy goes to a new occupant of an existing building, and sets fees of $10 for a zoning permit and $25 per dwelling unit for a certificate of occupancy. It does not use the words sale or resale, and no current resale form, checklist or fee sheet is posted, so the status is required with low confidence and the 1999 fees may be out of date. The Borough's Housing Code Official and Construction Code Official are Upper Deerfield Township staff (Teresa Warburton, 856-455-9591) under a shared service. Zoning Officer: the Other Officials page (updated February 2025) lists Norman Hetzell, 856-332-7332, while the Planning - Zoning page (updated September 2026) lists Daniel Lowe as Zoning Officer on the board. Neighboring Stow Creek Township, which shares the Housing office pattern, does require a CO on sale.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page and pick Shiloh Borough as the municipality. Payment is by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). The certificate is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 (guideline sheet) / (856) 451-0091 (Bureau of Fire Prevention).

fire_cert.notes: The DCA registry lists Shiloh Borough as F, and its shared-service note says Bridgeton City is the LEA for Shiloh; the City of Bridgeton Fire Department's own Uniform Fire Code page names Shiloh Borough, and its online smoke/CO application lists Shiloh Borough as a municipality choice. Fees, lead time and the 90-day validity come from the Bridgeton Bureau's guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025). The middle tier is printed as '7 business days prior'; the gap between 4 and 10 days is not spelled out. The guideline sheet lists no fire extinguisher (P.L.2025, c.19). Note: the Borough's 2025 reorganization agenda still lists 'SUPP. FIRE CODE OFFICIAL' and 'FIRE INSPECTION OFFICER' as Upper Deerfield Twp; the state registry (July 2026), the state directory and Bridgeton's own page all name Bridgeton as the fire enforcing agency. Firefighting is by interlocal agreement with Hopewell-Stow Creek Fire Co.; it does not issue certificates.
